mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened discount rates affecting future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: In a tightening cycle, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or the rise in FEDFUNDS is not confirmed by a decline in SPX 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) and a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggest labor market strengthening, which typically precedes S&P 500 gains over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in SPX over 60 days despite the labor indicators forming a statistically significant positive interaction (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in GDPC1 (goods orders) followed by a sustained increase in HOUST (home sales) over the next 5 days indicates accelerating business and consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns in the following week.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases then HOUST increases in the next 5 days
failure_condition: The 5-day SPX forward return is flat or negative despite the dual demand proxy moving in the predicted direction (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% while CPIAUCSL (inflation) remains below 0.2% suggests supply-side strength that supports S&P 500 gains over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day SPX return when the supply signal is present (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS increases, the S&P 500 exhibits negative 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate higher future borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: regime: FEDFUNDS consistently increasing for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% combined with a decline in PAYEMS suggests a weakening labor market, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS decreases in the following week
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) despite the labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 shows three consecutive monthly increases each exceeding 2%, the S&P 500 is expected to post positive 60-day forward returns as a signal of robust demand persistence.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly increases > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day SPX return when the demand momentum is detected (Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both INDPRO and RSAFS (residential construction) by more than 3% in the next month indicates supply contraction, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases > 3% and RSAFS decreases > 3% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day SPX forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when the supply contraction signal occurs.
